ShortDescription.Value: Wider pedestrian crossings, shaped one junction at a time, with a painted line down either side, plus diagonal crossings through the middle. Room for people to cross side by side.

Publish.LongDescription:
# Better Crosswalks
A crossing in Cities: Skylines II is a thin painted band that a queue of citizens shuffles across in single file. This mod widens the band and the strip people walk on together, so a crowd spreads out across it instead of filing over — and it lets you shape crossings one at a time, give them a painted border, or run them corner to corner through the middle of a junction.
## Width
One slider, as a percentage of whatever the crossing was drawn with rather than an absolute figure. Crossings are not uniform to begin with — a side street's is narrow, a boulevard's is not — and one absolute value would flatten that, so everything scales together and keeps its proportions. It starts at 150%, and goes from 25% to 400%.
A floor and a ceiling in metres are there for the cases where a proportion is not what you want: "no crossing narrower than 4m" is a sensible rule, "every crossing exactly 4m" usually is not.
## One junction at a time
The toolbar button opens a tool. Click a junction, then a crossing on it, and five rings appear on that crossing:
- either end — drag to swing that end up or down the road, for a crossing set at an angle rather than square across - the middle — drag to slide the whole crossing towards or away from the junction - either side — drag to pull it wider or narrower
Nothing you do to one crossing touches its neighbours. There are buttons too, if you would rather not drag: narrower and wider, "same for all the crossings here", and a reset for the crossing or for the whole junction. Everything set with the tool is saved with the city.
## Crossings through the middle
Junctions where four or more roads meet can take crossings corner to corner through the middle — a scramble crossing, the kind Shibuya is known for. They are on by default, and the tool edits and removes them like any other crossing. Turn them off in settings and any already in the city are cleared out.
## Lines down the sides
A solid line either side of the zebra stripes, so the crossing reads as a bordered band rather than a row of loose bars. The lines sit on the edge of the band and follow it, so a crossing you widen takes its borders with it.
Off out of the box, because it changes how every crossing in the city looks. The lines are the game's own road markings, laid by the game's own marking system, so they match whatever your roads are already painted with and nothing goes into your save. They appear only where the game paints a crossing — never on the unmarked ones, and never where there is no pavement to step onto, which is what a bridge usually has. A "Line style" dropdown picks between the markings found if the automatic choice is not the one you want. Crossings through the middle of a junction get lines too.
One thing to know: the game lays these lines when it builds a junction and saves them with your city, so a junction keeps the lines it was built with. On a city you already have, press "Apply to existing crossings and lines" once.
## How it works
A crossing is not part of the road's cross-section. It is a pedestrian lane laid across the carriageway, and the painted zebra is that lane's mesh. This mod writes the width of that lane on the lanes the game lays, and lets the game's own lane pipeline do everything else. No geometry of its own, no Harmony patches, and the road itself never gets wider.
Everything was worked out by decompiling and tracing the game's own assemblies. The full record — including the defects found in them, and the approaches that were tried and abandoned — is on the GitHub page.
## Applying it to a city you already have
Widths need nothing done. Change the setting and every crossing in the city follows immediately, including the ones already standing.
The lines are the exception, because the game lays those when it builds a junction and saves them with your city. Press "Apply to existing crossings and lines" once and every road is handed back to the game to be laid again, lines and all. Expect a pause on a large city.
## Removing it
Settings → Maintenance → "Remove this mod's data from the city", then save. Every crossing goes back to the width its asset author chose, every crossing this mod added is taken out, and the mod switches itself off so nothing puts them back before you save. The save is then exactly as it would have been if the mod had never run.
Publish.ChangeLog:
Lines down the sides of a crossing.
A new setting paints a solid line either side of the zebra stripes, so a crossing reads as a bordered band rather than a row of loose bars. The lines sit on the edge of the painted band and follow it, so a crossing you widen — with the slider or with the tool — takes its borders with it. Crossings through the middle of a junction get them too.
It is off out of the box. It changes how every crossing in the city looks, and unlike the width it is a matter of taste rather than of the crossing working better.
The lines are the game's own road markings, laid by the game's own marking system, so they are the paint your city's roads already use and nothing is added to your save. They appear only where the game paints a crossing: never on the unmarked ones it lays at every junction, and never where there is no pavement to step onto, which is what a bridge usually has. A "Line style" dropdown picks between the markings found, for the case where the automatic choice is not the one you want.
The game lays these lines when it builds a junction and saves them with your city, so a junction keeps the lines it was built with. On a city you already have, press "Apply to existing crossings and lines" once — every road is handed back to the game to be laid again. Expect a pause on a large city.
Also fixed: crossings through the middle of a junction built from divided roads ran to the median instead of to the far corner. A road with a median is crossed in two spans rather than one, and the mod was reading each span as a separate arm of the junction. This changes how many middle crossings such a junction has, so a width or a position you set by hand on one of them there starts again.
Widths, the crossing tool and everything else are unchanged.
